A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Forgetting method for supervised fine-tuning and retain matching core experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and rendered figures, tables, and equations support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark scores, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B, including reference-data duplication and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds results for Qwen2.5-3B and GPT-Neo-2.7B, additional benchmarks, and a constant-versus-adaptive forgetting-weight comparison.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 4–8 retain reference-model scoring, top-rho token selection, positive-token learning, and negative-token forgetting with the same linear weighting schedule. The additional discussion and experiments do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds instruction-following evaluation through IFEval, scientific reasoning through ARC-Challenge, contextual word prediction through LAMBADA, and mathematical computation through Arithmetic. These substantially broaden evaluation requirements beyond the retained five benchmarks; the five-source training corpus remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain Base, Full Tokens, Ignoring, and Forgetting, including the sequence-level and token-level variants in Table 3. New Table 8 extends the existing comparator set to additional settings. NPO and TNPO are discussed but are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds evaluation configurations using Qwen2.5-3B and GPT-Neo-2.7B, explicitly reusing the LLaMA-3.2-3B training setup. V4 specifies accuracy reporting for the new comparisons and OpenAI preprocessing for LAMBADA. The original training configurations, sample mixtures, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 expands the existing constant-versus-adaptive lambda analysis with Table 10 and a stated wider search over constants, although individual tested constants are not reported. Existing granularity, retention-rate, forgetting-rate, reference-duplication, and hyperparameter analyses remain; v1 Table 7 becomes v4 Table 9.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 6 retain means and standard deviations from three independent training runs. Other appendix results continue to use point estimates. V4 introduces no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports substantial additional results: Forgetting averages 59.01 versus Ignoring's 53.68 on Qwen2.5-3B, and 28.15 versus 24.59 on GPT-Neo-2.7B. Original benchmark tables and Figure 1 retain their values. Table 10 newly reports a constant-lambda average of 49.85, while Section 5.3 still states 49.59; the PDFs do not establish a comparable-setting improvement between those figures.

T1.justification: V4 removes all of Appendix C, including regularity and distributional assumptions, dynamic-regret and average-performance guarantees, linear-schedule optimality, DISDE-based reasoning, and generalization bounds and proofs. The main-text mathematical formulation remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central forgetting mechanism and performance/generalization claims remain. V4 removes the abstract's claim of experimentally demonstrated response diversity and explicitly emphasizes evaluation across model architectures. The conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: Removing Appendix C eliminates its substantial interpretation of forgetting through covariate-shift reduction, conditional-relationship preservation, and target-distribution coverage. Section 6 also replaces the warning about strong hyperparameter dependence with an explicit limitation concerning models beyond 13B parameters and larger training datasets. The main regularization explanation remains.

D1.justification: V4 documents reuse of the LLaMA-3.2-3B hyperparameters for the new model families and supplies LAMBADA preprocessing and dataset-access information. Existing LoRA settings, optimizer, hardware, software versions, training times, and evaluation-harness access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting the additional models, benchmarks, and LAMBADA preprocessing, while removing the DISDE reference and associated research connection with Appendix C. The main data-selection, unlearning, and preference-optimization positioning remains largely intact, with a more explicit NPO/TNPO comparison in Section 4.3.

P1.justification: Most shared prose and the main section order are retained. Editing is concentrated in the abstract, introduction, limitations, author header, and added explanatory passages. Appendix B is reorganized around the added experiments, and the theoretical appendix is removed.

P2.justification: V4 adds benchmark-description Table 7 and results Tables 8 and 10; the existing sensitivity table is renumbered as Table 9. Figure 1 retains identical plots but moves above the ablation discussion. Front matter and table placement are adjusted while the established visual format remains.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially improves evidential reliability by retaining the original experiments, adding evaluation beyond LLaMA, and withdrawing unreliable theoretical guarantees. V1's Theorem 3 proof ends with a term linear in training length despite its square-root regret claim, and Theorem 16's explanation says a nonnegative absolute-value term can become negative. Removing these arguments resolves substantive defects; narrowing the abstract and stating scaling limits further improves calibration. Table 10's unspecified constant and unexplained 49.85 versus 49.59 discrepancy remain limited reporting weaknesses.
